summary: A pattern a Type 3 glyph description paints with, stated in the font's (or the glyph stream's own) /Resources, is placed against the page's default coordinate space (or the enclosing form's), not against the glyph description's own. The interpreter swaps Interpreter::base, the space a pattern matrix maps to, at a form's Do, an imported page, an annotation appearance, a tiling cell and a soft mask's group, but not where a glyph description begins, although run() does reset the companion pattern_initial (§11.6.7) there. A glyph filling its square with a shading pattern draws the pattern's x 50 at the page's centre instead of its x 500.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.7.2: "Every pattern has a pattern matrix , a transformation matrix that maps the pattern's internal coordinate system to the default coordinate system of the pattern's parent content stream (the content stream in which the pattern is defined as a resource)." §8.3.2.4: "The transformation from pattern space to user space shall be specified by a pattern matrix contained in the pattern." Table 110 /Resources: the named resources "required by the glyph descriptions in this font"; §9.6.4: "When the glyph description begins execution, the current transformation matrix (CTM) shall be the concatenation of the font matrix ( FontMatrix in the current font dictionary) and the text space that was in effect at the time the text-showing operator was invoked". Errata Collection 3 Issue #128 (H7.8.3) puts the glyph stream's own /Resources first.

summary: On §10.8.3's simulated press under a CMYK output intent, DeviceGray is read as a one-component Separation whose colourant is named DeviceGray (intent_grey.rs, ADR 2758). A page may name a spot colourant /DeviceGray; the simulated device then has a plane of that name, SpotSet::available finds the construction's name among the planes, and every DeviceGray colour (fills, strokes, images, shadings) paints that spot plate at the grey value instead of the process black 1 - gray. With a cyan spot named /DeviceGray, '0.5 g' draws [128, 214, 247] where '0 0 0 0.5 k' draws [145, 143, 144].
source: ISO 32000-2 §10.2: "Colours specified in any device or CIE-based colour space shall be rendered as process colours." and "A device may also support additional spot colourants, which shall be painted only by means of Separation or DeviceN colour spaces that define such spot colourants." §10.3.2's DeviceGray to CMYK via §10.4.2.3.

summary: §10.8.3's simulation of a page with no CMYK output intent composites in the assumed inks (simulated_press and PagePress fall back to assumed_press), a device whose native colour space is CMYK, but output_intent::grey_reading answers GreyReading::Device there, so DeviceGray is separated into all four inks as a neutral by rgb_to_ink rather than converted by §10.4.2.3's method. source: ISO 32000-2 §10.3.2: "If the native device colour space is CMYK, then converting colours in the DeviceGray colour space to that CMYK should follow the method described in 10.4.2.3 , ' Conversion between DeviceGray and DeviceCMYK"." §10.4.2.3 (formula as Errata Collection 3 respells it, H10.4.2.3): cyan = magenta = yellow = 0.0, black = 1.0 - gray. §10.8.3 a): "The PDF processor determines what process colours and possible spot colours the simulated device is to have."
